solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fitting in again with leader of military ceremony

indicators.note: one word placed in another: the word for fitting sits inside the word for again

parts.note: bis is a call for a repeat, meaning again or twice
fitting means apt

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, so take the opening of military

explanation.surface: A neat fit being done once more alongside the head of a military ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fitting' looks like part of the ceremony, but it is the word APT; BIS, the call for an encore, is a convention for 'again'. 'in' places one inside the other; 'leader of' supplies M.
explanation.definitionFit: A baptism is a Christian rite of admission, a religious ceremony.

clue.text: Hit cover of Bellini at thunderous volume?

indicators.note: the cover of a word is its outside letters, so take the ends of the composer's name

parts.note: FF, fortissimo, is the musical direction for very loud

explanation.surface: A Bellini opera hit played at full blast.
explanation.definitionFit: Biff is informal for a punch or blow.

clue.text: Aide receiving a service and fabulous treatment

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so the aide's letters hold the others

parts.note: PA is a personal assistant, an aide
an is the indefinite article, like a
an ace is an unreturned service in tennis

explanation.surface: An assistant getting a tennis serve and wonderful care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fabulous' means mythical here, not marvellous.
explanation.definitionFit: A panacea is a legendary cure-all remedy, a treatment that exists only in fable.

clue.text: Kind of bond that's archetypal, caught only once

indicators.note: the word for archetypal has caught twice; keeping it only once drops one

parts.note: iconic means archetypal, a classic example
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A bond thought typical, yet caught just once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'only once' removes one of the two Cs in ICONIC.
explanation.definitionFit: An ionic bond is a chemical bond formed by attraction between charged ions.

clue.text: Wet suit off, with further clothing

indicators.note: clothing means covering, so the further word wraps the rearranged letters

parts.note: more means further, in addition

indicators.note: off means wrong or out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Taking a wet suit off and putting on more clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wet suit' reads as diving gear, but 'suit' is the fodder that 'off' rearranges, and 'clothing' wraps the result in the word for further. 'Wet' is a noun here.
explanation.definitionFit: Wet as a noun means dampness, liquid diffused in something.

clue.text: Cooler dance venue where lovers get together

parts.note: a fan is something that cools you
a club is a nightclub where people dance

explanation.surface: A trendier nightclub where couples meet up.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'lovers' are fans or devotees of some star, not romantic couples.
explanation.definitionFit: A fan club is a society where admirers of a celebrity gather.

clue.text: Official recalled film full of hot passion

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the official's letters are read backwards

parts.note: a ref, referee, is a match official
a vid is a video, a film

explanation.surface: A referee sent back to watch a heated replay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns REF into FER.
explanation.definitionFit: Fervid means intensely ardent or impassioned.

clue.text: Born writer tucked into tasty bit of bread once

indicators.note: tucked into means placed inside, so the born and writer pieces go within the tasty word

parts.note: nice means tasty or pleasant
NE, from French née, marks a maiden name, so born
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: A writer from birth enjoying a tasty morsel of bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bread' is slang for money, not food. NINEPENCE was a sum in Britain's pre-1971 currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread is slang for money, and ninepence was a small sum of old British money.

clue.text: Left part of Europe for part of Africa

parts.note: Iberia is the peninsula of Spain and Portugal

explanation.surface: Leaving one part of Europe for a part of Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberia is a country on the west coast of Africa.

clue.text: Attire for teen, one on beat boxes

parts.note: a bobby is a British policeman, who walks a beat
socks means punches, as a boxer does

explanation.surface: A teenager's outfit, and a patrolling officer who throws punches.
explanation.walkthrough: BOBBY is British slang for a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Bobby socks were ankle socks worn by teenage girls in 1940s and 1950s America.

clue.text: One may invest in more rococo houses

indicators.note: one word housing another holds it inside, here the comparative containing in

parts.note: rococo means elaborately ornate, so more rococo is fancier

explanation.surface: Someone putting money into grander, more ornate homes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'houses' is a verb meaning contains, not dwellings; 'in' is a literal piece, not a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A financier is a person whose business is putting money into ventures.

clue.text: New money must include a plutocrat

indicators.note: the outer letters must contain the inner one, signalling insertion

parts.note: a bob is old British slang for a shilling, so money

explanation.surface: Fresh cash has to be given to a rich man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must include' puts A inside N+BOB. A BOB was a shilling, an old British coin.
explanation.definitionFit: A nabob is a very wealthy person, originally one who made a fortune in India: a plutocrat.

clue.text: Boastful fixing end component where screwdriver may be had?

indicators.note: fixing here means holding firmly in place, so the boastful word grips the others inside it

parts.note: cocky means arrogantly boastful
the tail is the end of something
a part is a component

explanation.surface: A cocky mechanic fitting the end part of something, then reaching for a screwdriver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fixing' means holding in place, so the boastful word grips the other two. The screwdriver is the vodka-and-orange cocktail, not the tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A screwdriver is a mixed drink, the sort served at a drinks gathering.

clue.text: Second lot of ashes likely emptied with sadness

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second
an urnful is the amount an urn holds, as of cremated ashes

indicators.note: emptied means the middle is removed, leaving the outside letters

explanation.surface: A second batch of ashes probably being scattered sorrowfully.
explanation.definitionFit: Mournfully means sorrowfully, in a grieving manner.

clue.text: Track to follow round peaks where fruit grows

indicators.note: the track comes after, so its letters are placed at the end

parts.note: O is round in shape
a range is a chain of mountain peaks
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a track

explanation.surface: A path that circles around mountain tops to an orchard.
explanation.definitionFit: An orangery is a glazed building for growing citrus trees, so fruit is raised there.

clue.text: I see rifle almost raised in WWI campaign

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means written upwards, so everything is reversed

parts.note: lo is an old word for look, see

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: to rifle is to ransack or pillage

explanation.surface: Someone noticing a gun has nearly been lifted during a First World War battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts PILLAGE to PILLAG; 'raised' reverses ILOPILLAG.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallipoli was the 1915 Allied campaign against Ottoman Turkey in the First World War.

clue.text: Give a ring to prince returning figure welcomes

indicators.note: welcomes means takes in, so the prince goes inside
returning tells us to read the figure's letters backwards

parts.note: one is a figure, a number
Hal is Prince Hal, the young Henry V in Shakespeare

explanation.surface: Ringing a prince when a number returns to greet him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' applies to the figure, not the prince, giving ENO; 'welcomes' takes Shakespeare's Prince Hal inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To enhalo is to surround with a halo, a ring of light.

clue.text: Abroad, plonk last of bread on potato curry

parts.note: plonk is cheap wine, and vin is the French for wine

indicators.note: last of a word means its final letter, here of bread

parts.note: aloo is the Hindi word for potato, used on Indian menus

explanation.surface: Overseas, someone puts cheap wine and bread on a potato curry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potato' is wordplay, not part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Vindaloo is a fiery Indian dish from Goa, a kind of curry.

clue.text: Wave very gently, upset about that

indicators.note: about means going around, so the upset word surrounds the musical one

parts.note: to rile is to upset or annoy
PP, pianissimo, is the musical direction for very softly

explanation.surface: Waving very softly, then being upset by it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' is the verb to rile, not an anagram signal; 'about' wraps it round the musical marking. 'that' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A ripple is a small wave on water.

clue.text: It's a wonder Biblical figure blocks sink up

indicators.note: up in a down clue means written upwards, so the whole is reversed
blocks means stands in the way of, so she sits inside the word for sink

parts.note: to dip is to sink
Mary, mother of Jesus, is a Biblical figure

explanation.surface: A miracle when a Bible character stops a sink backing up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blocks' sets the Biblical figure inside the word for sink; 'up' then reverses everything, as this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The Great Pyramid of Giza is one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.

clue.text: A little work in green grass pile

parts.note: lime is a shade of green
a rick is a stack of hay, dried grass

explanation.surface: A spot of labour in a green field by a haystack.
explanation.definitionFit: A limerick is a short comic poem of five lines, a little literary work.

clue.text: Art of homeware dealer hemming raised collar

indicators.note: hemming means enclosing, so the store's name surrounds the other word

parts.note: Ikea is the Swedish home furnishings retailer

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means read upwards, so reversed

parts.note: to collar or nab is to arrest

explanation.surface: A homeware shop hemming a turned-up collar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collar' is a verb, to arrest; 'raised' reverses it as this is a down clue, and 'hemming' sets it inside the Swedish store's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ikebana is the Japanese art of flower arranging.

clue.text: Perhaps put polish on or polish off

definitions.meaning: to ... a surface is to give it a final coat, such as polish
to polish off is to ..., consume or complete

explanation.surface: Varnish something, or perhaps just get it done.
explanation.definitionFit: Finish means both applying a final coating and bringing something to an end.

clue.text: Travelling off, I repeatedly wintered in port?

indicators.note: travelling suggests moving about, so the letters change places

parts.note: repeatedly says the I just given comes again, supplying a second copy of it

explanation.surface: Someone who wintered in a harbour town after travelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeatedly' doubles I; 'Travelling' rearranges OFF+II+WINTERED. The question mark marks port as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Port is a sweet wine strengthened with added brandy, an example of the type.

clue.text: Dope's home telephone

parts.note: in means at home

explanation.surface: A fool's landline at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dope' is slang for information here, not a fool or drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Dope is informal for inside information, which intel is.

clue.text: Wave combination in pools

definitions.meaning: a permanent wave in the hair

explanation.surface: A wave pattern in swimming pools.
explanation.walkthrough: The football pools are a British betting game on match results.
explanation.definitionFit: Perm is short for both permanent wave and permutation.

clue.text: Period of waiting in car without book

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the car's letters go around the book

parts.note: a limo is a limousine, a car

explanation.surface: A spell of waiting in a vehicle with nothing to read.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here: LIMO goes round B.
explanation.definitionFit: Limbo is an uncertain state of waiting for something to be resolved.

clue.text: I'm going to answer guy that's awkward

parts.note: I'll is short for I will, meaning I'm going to
to guy is to mock or tease

explanation.surface: Someone about to respond to an awkward man.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling ill at ease means being uncomfortable or embarrassed, socially awkward.

clue.text: German's relative has handy habit around food

indicators.note: around here means turned round, read backwards

parts.note: DIY, do-it-yourself, is the habit of handy people
a dish is a serving of food

explanation.surface: A relative from Germany who is handy and has a habit around food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'handy habit' is do-it-yourself; 'around' turns those initials backwards. 'German's relative' means a language related to German.
explanation.definitionFit: Yiddish is a language that grew from medieval High German, a relative of German.

clue.text: Old hand in part shepherds one learner: it may bear fruit

indicators.note: split in part, the old hand guards the others between its pieces as shepherds guard a flock

parts.note: the palm is part of the hand, standing for it
I is the Roman numeral one
L is for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: An experienced shepherd, partly employed, guiding one trainee who may succeed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in part shepherds' splits O+PALM to hold I+L between them.
explanation.definitionFit: The oil palm is a tree grown for its oily fruit.
